Summary

First draft of Maser's design documentation in docs/design/, modeled on IEC 62304 (software lifecycle), ISO 14971 (risk management) and IEC 62366 (usability), for practice. It covers the features in main as of #16.

Document Contents
README.md Index, ID scheme, how references and changes work
software-development-plan.md Scope and intended use, a practice safety class (B) with its rationale, lifecycle, SOUP, configuration management, verification strategy
user-needs.md UN-1 to UN-10
requirements.md 52 requirements in 9 areas. Each one lists its need, its risk control and its verification: existing tests, a record, inspection, or a named gap.
risk-management.md 6 harms, the scales and acceptability matrix, 17 hazards with initial and residual risk, 20 controls, residual risk evaluation, and the open risks
usability.md Use specification, safety-related UI characteristics, 8 hazard-related use scenarios, this week's hand testing recorded as formative evaluations FE-1 to FE-6, and a summative evaluation plan
traceability.md Needs → requirements, hazards → controls → requirements, coverage counts, and the next steps (trace checker, test IDs, UI harness)

AGENTS.md now requires behavior changes to update these documents in the same PR.

Findings

Writing the risk file turned up risks that aren't controlled yet. Each is now an issue, and the proposed controls are Proposed requirements:

  • #18 (HAZ-02, residual High): line comments and reviews aren't pinned to a commit. If someone pushes after Maser loads the diff, a comment can land on a different line, and an Approve covers commits the reviewer never saw. Until this is fixed, the file rates Maser not acceptable for review at work.
  • #19 (HAZ-07): unsent text is lost on a crash or quit.
  • #20 (HAZ-04/05/10): nothing names the PR or the GitHub account when posting. Finish Review doesn't say which PR it submits to.
  • #21 (HAZ-12): gh calls have no timeout.

For review

This is a first draft that you should read and challenge. Things I'd most like your view on:

  • The severity scale and acceptability matrix in risk-management.md.
  • The safety class rationale in software-development-plan.md: Class A on a strict reading, treated as Class B for practice.
  • Whether the user needs read like yours.
  • The overall residual risk statement: acceptable for personal use, not yet for work.

Testing

Documentation only. The coverage counts in traceability.md were produced by a script that reads the requirements table, not counted by hand.
